title: Kafka: Event Streaming
blurb: Topics, partitions, consumer groups, replication and delivery guarantees
summary: Kafka is a distributed, durable log. Producers append events to topics, which are split into partitions spread across brokers; consumers read them at their own pace and remember where they are with offsets. It decouples services, absorbs traffic spikes, and lets many systems react to the same events.

nodes.label: orders.DLQ (dead letters)
nodes.subtitle: A topic for events that keep…

steps.title: Producer (Order Service)
steps.text: The Order Service produces an "order paid" event to the orders topic, keyed by the order id, with acks=all.

steps.title: Partitioner (hash of key)
steps.text: The partitioner hashes the key with murmur2 and takes it modulo 3: every event for order-1001 lands on partition 0, so they stay in order.
steps.data:
murmur2("order-1001") = 297523878
(297523878 & 0x7fffffff) % 3 = 0
→ partition 0, leader: Broker 1 · P0 leader

steps.title: Broker 1 · P0 leader
steps.text: Broker 1 · P0 leader appends the event to the end of partition 0's log at offset 48210. A partition is just an append-only file: writes are sequential, which is why Kafka is fast.

steps.title: Broker 1 · P0 leader → Broker 2 · P1 leader
steps.text: With acks=all, the leader waits until the in-sync replicas (here Broker 2) have copied it, then confirms. min.insync.replicas=2 means two copies exist before the producer hears "done".
steps.data:
replication.factor=3, min.insync.replicas=2
ISR(orders-0) = [1, 2, 3]
ack → producer after 2 of 3 replicas have offset 48210

steps.title: Billing Consumer 1
steps.text: In the billing group, partition 0 belongs to Billing Consumer 1. Each partition has exactly one consumer per group, so the order's events are handled in order, by one consumer.
steps.data:
group billing: P0, P1 → Billing Consumer 1; P2 → Billing Consumer 2
poll() → [offset 48210] order-1001

steps.title: Billing Consumer 1 → Billing DB
steps.text: Billing Consumer 1 creates the invoice in the Billing DB, idempotently, so a retry could never charge twice.
steps.data:
INSERT INTO invoices (order_id, amount_inr) VALUES ('order-1001', 1499)
ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO NOTHING;

steps.title: Billing Consumer 1 → __consumer_offsets
steps.text: Then it commits offset 48211 to __consumer_offsets: "next time, start after this event".

steps.title: Analytics Consumer
steps.text: Separately, the Analytics Consumer reads the same event at its own pace. Consumer groups don't take events away from each other: each group has its own offsets.
steps.data: group analytics, orders-0: committed offset 45779 (it's behind, and that's fine)

takeaways: A topic is split into partitions: append-only logs spread across brokers.
The key decides the partition, and order is only guaranteed within a partition.
Each partition goes to one consumer per group; more partitions means more parallel consumers.
acks=all with min.insync.replicas=2 is what keeps a broker crash from losing events.
